ga.text: (b) We recorded charges of $17 million and $21 million during the quarters ended March 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, to General and administrative expenses related to a resource optimization program. Over the past several years, this program has allowed us to reallocate significant resources to accelerate our digital, technology and innovation capabilities to deliver a modern, world-class team member and customer experience and improve unit economics. We expanded the program in 2024 to identify further opportunities to optimize the Company’s spending and identify additional, critical areas in which to potentially reallocate resources, both with a goal to enable the acceleration of the Company’s growth rate. lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In 2025, our system restaurants generated digital sales approaching both $40 billion and 60% of overall system sales.
Our long-term growth depends on maintaining the pace of our new unit growth rate largely through our Concepts’ franchisees.
We also rely on master franchisees, who have rights to license to sub-franchisees the right to develop and operate restaurants, to achieve our expectations for new unit development.

We have limited control over how our Concepts’ franchisees’ businesses are run, and their inability to operate successfully could adversely affect our operating results through decreased royalties, advertising funds contributions, and fees paid to us for other discrete services we may provide to our Concepts’ franchisees Our control is further limited where we utilize master franchise arrangements, which require us to rely on our master franchisees to enforce sub-franchisee compliance with our operating standards.
Our growth strategy depends upon our and our Concepts’ franchisees ’ ability to successfully open new restaurants and to operate these restaurants profitably.
Our growth strategy depends on our and our Concepts’ franchisees’ ability to increase the number of restaurants around the world.
We own and manage some of these IT Systems but also rely on third parties for a range of IT Systems and related products and services.
Much of our future success depends on the continued availability and service of senior management personnel.
If any of these facts, assumptions, representations or undertakings are incorrect or not satisfied, we may not be able to rely on these opinions of outside counsel.
We believe gross unit openings and net new unit growth are useful to investors because we depend on new units for a significant portion of our growth.

In instances where we rely on third parties to provide goods or services to franchisees at our direction, we have determined we act as a principal in these transactions and recognize related revenues as the goods or services are transferred to the franchisee.
The funding rules for our pension plans outside of the U.S. vary from country to country and depend on many factors including discount rates, performance of plan assets, local laws and regulations.

The actual number of shares of common stock to be received and sold following the exercise of the awards will depend upon the appreciation in the value of the awards and the number of shares withheld for any taxes.
Changes in the fair value of our ownership interest in Devyani prior to the date of sale resulted in pre-tax investment losses of

Changes in the fair value of our ownership interest in Devyani prior to the date of sale resulted in pre-tax investment losses of $ 20 million in the year ended December 31, 2024 and pre-tax investment income of $ 8 million in the year ended December 31, 2023 (see Note 14).

During the quarter ended March 31, 2024, we sold our approximate 5% minority investment in Devyani International Limited (“Devyani”), a franchise entity that operates KFC and Pizza Hut restaurants in India, for pre-tax proceeds of $ 104 million.

The change was primarily driven by higher current year spending on restaurant acquisitions, higher current year capital spending and lapping prior year proceeds arising from the sale of our approximate 5% minority investment in Devyani, partially offset by maturities of short-term investments in the current year compared to net purchases of short-term investments in the prior year.
